title: onboarding registers a project inside the engine's existing projects: block even when its header carries a comment, never appends a second block, and stays idempotent
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05 firstmate onboarded the pilot external project with `bin/fm-onboard.sh add <external project path> --name the pilot external project --answers <file>` (same as `bin/fm-project.sh add`). `register()` in bin/lib/fm_onboard.py:325-338 looks for the registry block with `^projects:\s*$` (:334), but the engine's config.yaml header is `projects:               # every repository firstmate drives; design section 15.2` (config.yaml:73, a trailing comment). The search failed, so register() took the `else` branch (:336-337) and appended a second `projects:` block at the end of the file. The registry reader (`top_block` in bin/lib/fm_registry.py:37-49) reads only the first column-0 `projects:` block, so `fm_project_get the pilot external project github` said the project was not registered. Firstmate moved the entry under the real block by hand; that working-tree change to config.yaml is not committed and this task does not touch it. The same `^  <name>:\s*$` pattern (fm_onboard.py:329 in register() and :400 in main()) misses an entry line that carries a trailing comment, so an existing name with a comment is not recognised.

Header match, one rule with the reader. register() finds the registry header with the same rule as `top_block` in bin/lib/fm_registry.py:42: a column-0 line matching `projects:\s*(#.*)?$`. Count the matching column-0 lines in config.yaml: (a) more than one: raise ValueError('config.yaml has more than one projects: block; merge them by hand before onboarding') and write nothing (the file stays byte-identical); (b) exactly one: insert the entry inside that block as defined in the next item; (c) none: append `\nprojects:\n` plus the entry at the end of the file, as today (:337). The entry text is unchanged (:333: two-space name line, then `github`, `base`, `required_check` at four spaces, values JSON-quoted). register() keeps its signature (engine, name, p) and its only production caller (fm_onboard.py:408).

Where the entry goes. The block body uses the reader's boundary rule (fm_registry.py:44-46): after the header, blank lines and lines whose stripped text starts with `#` are skipped, and the block ends at the first other line whose first character is not whitespace (or at end of file). register() inserts the entry immediately after the last line inside the block whose first character is whitespace (an indented entry line or an indented comment continuation such as config.yaml:82-85); if the block has no indented line, directly after the header. The text before and after the insertion point is unchanged byte for byte, and the inserted text always starts on a new line and ends with a newline (when the line before the insertion point lacks a final newline, one is added). A following top-level key (for example a later `default_project:` or a column-0 comment that precedes it) stays after the new entry.

Existing names. Both name checks (fm_onboard.py:329 in register() and :400 in main()) match `^  <name>:[ \t]*(#.*)?$`, so an entry line with a trailing comment is recognised. Behaviour for an existing name is unchanged: when its registered `github` and `base` equal the proposed ones, register() writes nothing (re-onboarding is idempotent and the file stays byte-identical); when either differs, main() still raises 'existing registry binding differs; choose a different name' (:403) and register() still raises 'existing registry binding differs' (:331); the self project (`repo: .`) still cannot be replaced (:404-405). `required_check` of an existing entry is not compared or rewritten (as today).

Tests, in a new suite tests/onboard-register.test.sh (sources tests/lib.sh, uses `safe_tmpdir`, unsets FM_*/HERDR_*/GH_REPO like tests/onboard-cli.test.sh:4, sets FM_HOME to a temp dir, drives `bin/fm-project.sh add <empty folder> --name <n> --repo <engine> --answers <file>` with the answers shape of tests/onboard-cli.test.sh:17-19, and reads routing back with `fm_project_get` through bin/fm-config.sh). Use only tests/lib.sh assertions (assert_eq, assert_ok, assert_contains, assert_lacks); no `assert_*` names from unittest.mock in this .sh file. The engine fixture copies the real header shape: `projects:               # every repository firstmate drives; design section 15.2`, a self entry `  self:` with `repo: .`, `github`, `base`, `required_check`, a nested `policy:` map and an indented comment continuation line starting at column 24 with `#`, like config.yaml:73-85. Cases: (a) commented header: add `seed`; exit 0; exactly one column-0 `projects:` line; `fm_project_get seed github` and `base` return the answers; every line of the self entry is unchanged (compare the fixture's self lines before and after). (b) block followed by a top-level key: the fixture has `default_project: self` after the block; after add, the seed entry sits before `default_project:` and `fm_project_get seed github` works. (c) two blocks: a fixture with two column-0 `projects:` lines; add exits non-zero, stderr contains 'more than one projects: block', and config.yaml is byte-identical (cmp). (d) idempotent: run the same add twice on the commented-header fixture; the second run exits 0 and leaves config.yaml byte-identical to after the first. (e) existing name with a trailing comment: a fixture entry `  seed:   # pilot` bound to another github; add for `seed` with different answers exits non-zero with 'existing registry binding differs' and leaves the file byte-identical. (f) no block: config.yaml `vendor: mock` only; add appends one `projects:` block and the entry (regression guard; tests/onboard-cli.test.sh:10-12 covers this too).

Callers and suites to keep green (grep `fm_onboard` over bin/ and tests/ lists exactly these). Production: bin/fm-onboard.sh:5 (execs fm_onboard.py) and bin/fm-project.sh add/edit; bin/lib/fm_conventions_watch.py:13 (imports atomic, drift, inspect_remote, registry_value, save; not register); bin/fm-canary.sh:670 (infer, approve). Direct callers of the changed insertion path, which stay green under the new rule: (1) tests/conventions-watch.test.sh:45-64 imports `fm_onboard as O` and runs `O.main(['add', ..., '--name', 'new', ...])` on a fixture `default_project: self` + `projects:` with entries self, one, two (:30-36) and asserts `'  new:'` is in config.yaml (:61); the new entry now goes after `two` at the end of the block instead of directly after the header, and the assertion still holds. (2) tests/onboard-remote.test.sh: its fixture (:14) is `default_project: self`, `projects:`, `  self:`; `agent` is now placed after `self` (at the end of the block) instead of before it; :38 `sed -n '/  agent:/,/  self:/p'` then prints from `  agent:` to the end of the file, which still holds only agent's four lines, so it still reads `base github required_check`; the later append of `  empty:` at :63-68 lands after agent inside the block; the self-replacement refusal (:42-44) and the binding-differs refusal (:45-49) are unchanged. (3) tests/onboard-cli.test.sh:10-12 (`vendor: mock` only: path (c), append, unchanged). Importers that do not reach register() (infer/approve/edit/inspect only), unaffected: tests/onboarding.test.sh:24, tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh:17 and :83, tests/project.test.sh:213, tests/external-reviews.test.sh:248, tests/conventions-publication.test.sh:72, tests/external-review-launchers.test.sh:12, tests/external-review-entrypoint.test.sh:12, tests/lib/external_entrypoints.py:15, tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py:587, tests/lib/external_stock.py:15. bin/lib/fm_registry.py is read, not changed. Note: a refused add (two blocks, or a differing binding) still runs approve() first (fm_onboard.py:407), so it may already have written CONVENTIONS.md under FM_HOME; this task promises only that the engine config.yaml stays byte-identical on refusal.

How a registry entry reaches main (no code change). The engine config.yaml is a tracked, public file that carries routing only (design §15.2, 'T-139 private onboarding contract'). Firstmate has no git write, and onboarding only edits the engine checkout's working tree. design.md already routes a captain's config choice through 'a `config.yaml` pull request' (§5.3, design/design.md:590-595, the reviewer/worker vendor paragraph). So the routing entry written by onboarding reaches main through a pull request: the operator step is to carry the exact entry in a captain-approved change (for example the external pilot task's PR when its scope allows config.yaml, or a dedicated one-file PR), never by a firstmate commit. Until it lands, routing works from the engine checkout's working tree only. Document this in place in design §15.2, in the 'T-139 private onboarding contract' paragraph (design/design.md:4958-4970), after the sentence 'The public engine registry carries routing only; …': one sentence that onboarding inserts the routing entry into the existing `projects:` block (a trailing comment allowed; a second block is refused) and one sentence that the entry is a working-tree change to the tracked config.yaml that reaches main only through a pull request. Nothing is appended at the end of design.md (T-189).

In flight and migration. No stored record changes shape. The the pilot external project entry in the engine config.yaml was already moved under the real block by hand; this task neither reads nor rewrites that working-tree change (the worker's worktree config.yaml is main's, without it). A config.yaml that already carries a duplicate `projects:` block from the old bug makes the next `add` refuse with the new message; the operator merges the blocks by hand. Onboardings already completed are unaffected; re-running `add` for an already registered name with the same binding is a no-op.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from tests/onboard-register.test.sh: cases a, b, c, d and e are red on base (a, b, d: base appends a second block and the name is not registered; c: base inserts into the first block instead of refusing; e: base's name pattern misses the commented line, so it appends a second entry block); f is a regression guard that also holds on base. No vendor stub is involved: no GitHub call is made for a local empty folder (bin/lib/fm_onboard.py inspect_local).
